Nadab and Abihu
NAY-dab and uh-BYE-hew
proper noun
From the Hebrew: Nadab, “liberal” or “willing”; Abihu, “he is my father.”

📖 Biblical Definition

Nadab and Abihu were the two eldest sons of Aaron, set apart with their father and brothers to minister in the priest’s office. They had been granted a great privilege: with Moses and Aaron and the seventy elders they went up the mount, saw the God of Israel, and did eat and drink in His presence. Yet privilege did not breed reverence. Soon after the tabernacle was consecrated and fire from the LORD had consumed the offering, these two sons took each his censer, put fire therein, and laid incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the LORD, which He commanded them not. The judgment was immediate and terrible: there went out fire from the LORD and devoured them, and they died before the LORD. Moses declared the meaning to Aaron: I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified; and Aaron held his peace. Their bodies were carried out of the camp in their coats by their cousins, and the priests were forbidden to mourn lest wrath fall upon the whole congregation. Some have linked their presumption to wine, for the very next command forbade priests strong drink when they went into the tabernacle. Nadab and Abihu stand forever as the warning of profane worship—men who approached the holy God on their own terms and were consumed.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Aaron’s two eldest sons, who offered strange fire before the LORD and were devoured by fire from His presence.

expand to see more

NADAB AND ABIHU, the two eldest sons of Aaron, set apart to the priesthood.

They saw the God of Israel on the mount with Moses and the elders (Exo 24:9).

They offered strange fire before the LORD, which He commanded them not (Lev 10:1).

Fire went out from the LORD and devoured them, and they died.

They died childless, and the priesthood continued through Eleazar and Ithamar (Num 3:4).

📖 Key Scripture

Lev 10:1 — "And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not."

Lev 10:2 — "And there went out fire from the LORD, and devoured them, and they died before the LORD."

Lev 10:3 — "Then Moses said unto Aaron, This is it that the LORD spake, saying, I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace."

Num 3:4 — "And Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD, when they offered strange fire before the LORD, in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children: and Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest’s office in the sight of Aaron their father."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Nadab and Abihu are the enduring warning against will-worship—approaching God in any way He has not commanded.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The lesson to recover is the holiness of God and the peril of self-devised worship. Their fire was strange because the LORD commanded it not; they offered what seemed good in their own eyes rather than what God had appointed, and they were consumed. The regulative principle—that God is to be worshipped only as He has prescribed—is written in their ashes.

Their fall confronts the modern appetite for worship shaped by feeling, novelty, and the worshipper’s own preference. God will be sanctified in them that come nigh Him; He is not honored by sincerity in disobedience. The nearer the privilege, the greater the accountability: these men had seen God and yet trifled with His holiness. Reverence, not innovation, befits those who draw near to a consuming fire.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The brothers’ names speak of willingness and fatherhood, in tragic irony to their willful, fatal presumption.

expand to see more

Nadab — Hebrew, “liberal,” “willing,” or “noble.”

Abihu — Hebrew, “he is my father” or “my father is he.”

They were the first and second sons of Aaron by Elisheba.

The “strange fire” was fire and incense not commanded by the LORD.

They died childless, so their line did not continue the priesthood.

Usage

"Like Nadab and Abihu, those who worship God on their own terms invite His judgment."

"The strange fire of Nadab and Abihu stands against every self-devised act of worship."

"God was sanctified in Nadab and Abihu, and Aaron held his peace."
